basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 10.' and it opens 'Vers. 10. Circumcidetur omne masculinum in vobis. Jure Abraham lex ista constituta est'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 10. Circumcidetur omne masculinum in vobis. Jure Abraham lex ista constituta est ut, quia primus homo per praevaricationem mandatorum Dei displicuerat, Abraham signum foederis esset inter Deum et hominem. Secundo, ut per hanc a caeteris nationibus discernerentur in corporibus. Tertio, ut hanc eo membro suscipientes in quo dominari | libido solet discerent castitatem sibi servandam et omnem impudicitiam recidendam.
